question: Can I work while studying on a student visa?
answer:
Yes, you can work while studying on a student visa, but there are some conditions. 

If you are studying a master's degree by research or doctoral degree, or your family members are with you, you can work more than 48 hours a fortnight (Source: 500_when_have.pdf, p.3). However, if you are studying a master's degree by coursework, or a master's degree (Extended), you and your family members can still work more than 48 hours a fortnight (Source: 500_when_have.pdf, p.3).

question: What do I need to arrange if I am under 18 and applying for a student visa?
answer: If you are under 18 years old and applying for a Student visa, you must have appropriate welfare arrangements in place. These arrangements must cover your period of stay or until you turn 18 years, whichever is first (Source: 500_steps.pdf, p.11). Additionally, you must have consent from your parent(s) or guardian(s) to travel to and reside in Australia as an under 18 student (Source: 500_steps.pdf, p.11). You will also need to provide a completed and signed consent Form 1229 (Source: 500_steps.pdf, p.11) or a statutory declaration from each parent or legal guardian.
